original_items.title: Submodel information aspect
original_items.native_meaning: Submodel is a globally identifiable information aspect of the represented asset; submodelElement has cardinality 0..*.
original_items.caveat: An information group is not an installed subsystem.

original_items.title: Template and instance
original_items.native_meaning: Submodel kind propagates template/instance interpretation to contained elements. semanticId is recommended. Validators treat Submodel like a collection rather than a list.
original_items.caveat: No new DIM class hierarchy or physical asset-kind rule follows.

original_items.title: SubmodelElement abstract base
original_items.native_meaning: Abstract SubmodelElement inherits Referable, HasSemantics, Qualifiable and HasDataSpecification. A semanticId is recommended; semantic property-definition attributes may need an external lookup.
original_items.caveat: The base is not an observation, command, physical component or proof of interoperability.

original_items.title: Optional values
original_items.native_meaning: Value-related attributes are typically optional so the same structures can describe templates.
original_items.caveat: A missing value is not a measured zero or an explicit empty update.

original_items.title: Property
original_items.native_meaning: A single-value DataElement has required valueType, optional value and optional coded-value reference valueId.
original_items.caveat: Property is broader than a measured observable; subject, timing and source are not established by this class alone.

original_items.title: MultiLanguageProperty
original_items.native_meaning: A DataElement can carry a multilingual value and optional valueId.
original_items.caveat: Translated value text is distinct from a field display label and from separate measurements.

original_items.title: Range
original_items.native_meaning: Range has required valueType and optional min/max values; the class is explicitly Experimental.
original_items.caveat: This alone does not define allowed/excluded values, endpoint inclusion, calibration limits or measured uncertainty.

original_items.title: File locator
original_items.native_meaning: File is a DataElement whose optional value is an absolute or relative file URI; contentType is optional. Package-relative interpretation is explained.
original_items.caveat: A file locator does not prove file access, media acquisition, observation association or AASX package conformance.

original_items.title: Embedded Blob
original_items.native_meaning: Blob stores file content directly in its optional value; contentType is optional.
original_items.caveat: Embedded bytes and an external file locator are different representations.

original_items.title: ReferenceElement
original_items.native_meaning: A DataElement holds an optional logical reference within/across shells or an external reference.
original_items.caveat: A reference is not evidence of a cable, physical attachment or reachable network service.

original_items.title: RelationshipElement endpoints and meaning
original_items.native_meaning: semanticId supplies relationship meaning. first is the subject reference and second the object reference; each is 0..1 in v3.2. AnnotatedRelationshipElement SHALL be used when the semantic definition requires information outside the endpoints.
original_items.caveat: Do not import older-edition required endpoints or infer physical part-of from this general relation.

original_items.title: AnnotatedRelationshipElement
original_items.native_meaning: Adds 0..* DataElement annotations to a relationship; the annotations qualify the relationship between its endpoints.
original_items.caveat: The annotation vocabulary and relationship meaning still require source evidence.

original_items.title: Entity and statements
original_items.native_meaning: Entity models parts of composite assets such as a bill of materials. Statements are 0..* SubmodelElements; entityType and globalAssetId are 0..1, specificAssetId 0..*.
original_items.caveat: Design composition does not prove installed configuration. Empty Inherits-from prose is qualified using pinned schema and local diagram sources.

original_items.title: Co-managed and self-managed entities
original_items.native_meaning: CoManagedEntity has no separate shell and belongs to a self-managed entity; SelfManagedEntity has its own shell and may also belong to a composite self-managed entity.
original_items.caveat: Shell-management boundaries do not establish device taskability, physical independence or native CSAPI subsystem rules.

original_items.title: Collection named structure
original_items.native_meaning: SubmodelElementCollection groups multiple named values, typically a semantically predefined set. Members are not ordered and have unique idShort names; following template order is recommended. value is 0..*.
original_items.caveat: Not an installed component container or a guarantee that every member has a distinct semanticId.

original_items.title: List structure
original_items.native_meaning: SubmodelElementList stores a zero-indexed sequence with required typeValueListElement; orderRelevant is optional with default true. Optional semanticIdListElement/valueTypeListElement qualify children; value is 0..*.
original_items.caveat: The prose discusses sets and bags, but orderRelevant alone does not prove uniqueness or define ISA min/max length and tree-depth bounds.

original_items.title: Recursive information examples
original_items.native_meaning: Lists of lists can represent multidimensional arrays; collections of column lists can represent tables; a list of collections can represent documents.
original_items.caveat: Publisher structural examples are not observed equipment trees or a mandated common Details-view layout.

original_items.title: List naming and reference position
original_items.native_meaning: References distinguish model and external targets, retain ordered keys, and may carry a recommended semantic expectation. References must not be treated as locators.
original_items.caveat: Exact reference-chain and list-position rules are separately recorded; full reference examples/algorithms remain outside this increment.

original_items.title: Semantic identifiers
original_items.native_meaning: HasSemantics provides optional main semanticId and 0..* supplementalSemanticId; supplemental IDs require a main ID under AASd-118.
original_items.caveat: The AAS02 overview-versus-cardinality wording question remains open; no mandatory universal semanticId is adopted.

original_items.title: ConceptDescription
original_items.native_meaning: ConceptDescription defines semantics, is Identifiable, uses data specifications and may reference compatible/derived external definitions via isCaseOf 0..*. Prose expects at least one data specification.
original_items.caveat: isCaseOf does not establish exact equivalence. The inherited reference cardinality and prose expectation need contextual validation, not an invented DIM SHALL.

original_items.title: Data specification versus Submodel template
original_items.native_meaning: A data specification template defines additional attributes, has a globally unique ID and content, and belongs to separately maintained specifications. Several templates can apply.
original_items.caveat: It differs from a Submodel template; the Part 1 IEC 61360 diagram is expressly non-normative and does not audit Part 3a/3b.

original_items.title: HasDataSpecification
original_items.native_meaning: An element references 0..* data specification templates by global ID.
original_items.caveat: Normal JSON uses embeddedDataSpecifications instead; concept-description prose does not make the inherited generic cardinality universally mandatory.

original_items.title: Qualifier and three kinds
original_items.native_meaning: Qualifier has required type/valueType and optional value/valueId. ValueQualifier concerns an instance value, ConceptQualifier the semantic definition, and TemplateQualifier template metadata; kind defaults to ConceptQualifier and the attribute is Experimental.
original_items.caveat: Quality, as-planned/as-maintained and mandatory/optional examples need actual qualifier definitions. External IEC/DIN sources and the embedded image are not audited here.

original_items.title: Template identifier provenance
original_items.native_meaning: AdministrativeInformation.templateId records which template guided creation; its note directs validation to Submodel.semanticId instead.
original_items.caveat: Creation provenance is not a complete template-validation contract.

original_items.title: Normal JSON empty aggregation rule
original_items.native_meaning: Normal JSON forbids empty aggregation arrays; an empty aggregation is represented by omitting the attribute. Singular metamodel association names generally become plural JSON keys.
original_items.caveat: This representation does not preserve ISA supplied-empty versus omitted-update distinctions by itself; Part 2 update behavior remains unreviewed.

original_items.title: Normal JSON value representation
original_items.native_meaning: Property.value and Range.min/max are JSON strings interpreted using valueType; BlobType uses base64. ValueOnly is a different representation; round trips may change lexical form.
original_items.caveat: Native encoding is not a new DIM datatype; full ValueOnly/XML/RDF behavior is not audited here.

original_items.title: Discriminator and embedded specifications
original_items.native_meaning: Normal JSON uses allOf for inherited constraints, modelType as a serialization discriminator, and embeddedDataSpecifications rather than the metamodel dataSpecification reference attribute.
original_items.caveat: modelType is expressly not a metamodel attribute. Serialization mechanics are retained as native evidence, not universal equipment fields.

original_items.title: Semantic matching strategies
original_items.native_meaning: The annex distinguishes exact-reference matching, value matching and knowledge-dependent compatible matching. Examples may require edition/dictionary knowledge; one proposed mapping is explicitly only a candidate.
original_items.caveat: Matching labels or identifier text does not prove exact semantic equivalence. Full reference algorithm and external dictionaries are unreviewed.

original_items.title: Operation structural boundary
original_items.native_meaning: Operation has three 0..* variable collections. OperationVariable wraps exactly one SubmodelElement; variable idShort values must be unique. Cardinality/default extensions are described as future possibilities.
original_items.caveat: Structure read here; invocation, outcomes, authorization and CSAPI Command comparison are deferred to AAS04/Part 2 review.

original_items.title: Capability structural boundary
original_items.native_meaning: Capability expresses implementation-independent potential to achieve an effect; the note discusses semantic links to skills.
original_items.caveat: Do not infer current readiness, implementation or achieved effect. Capability meaning/comparison is AAS04.

original_items.title: Experimental event structures
original_items.native_meaning: BasicEventElement has observed/direction/state, optional messaging and interval fields; EventPayload has event-source/scope references and a trigger timestamp. EventPayload is outside AASX information-model exchange according to its note.
original_items.caveat: Read as element inventory only here. Event lifecycle, lastUpdate versus trigger time and interface semantics are deferred to AAS04/Part 2; no observation-equivalence claim.

original_items.title: Abstract DataElement and EventElement
original_items.native_meaning: DataElement is not composed of other SubmodelElements and carries a value or predefined number of values. Categories are deprecated.
original_items.caveat: Abstract classes are not concrete JSON choice alternatives; EventElement separately remains abstract and Experimental.

original_items.title: Element-type enumeration
original_items.native_meaning: AasSubmodelElements lists both abstract and concrete types, while the original JSON SubmodelElement_choice contains 14 concrete alternatives.
original_items.caveat: An enumeration count is not a count of adopted DIM classes. Native type grammar and per-instance conformance remain distinct.

original_constraint_items.native_meaning: Property value and coded value must agree when both are present.
original_constraint_items.caveat: Native AAS constraint only; not an adopted DIM/Profile requirement or proof of schema enforcement.

original_constraint_items.native_meaning: Each language value must have the meaning of the referenced coded value.
original_constraint_items.caveat: Native AAS constraint only; not an adopted DIM/Profile requirement or proof of schema enforcement.

original_constraint_items.native_meaning: SelfManagedEntity requires globalAssetId or specificAssetId.
original_constraint_items.caveat: Native AAS constraint only; not an adopted DIM/Profile requirement or proof of schema enforcement.

original_constraint_items.native_meaning: Qualifier type must be unique within a qualifiable element.
original_constraint_items.caveat: Native AAS constraint only; not an adopted DIM/Profile requirement or proof of schema enforcement.

original_constraint_items.native_meaning: Non-identifiable idShort names are unique within their namespace, case-sensitive.
original_constraint_items.caveat: Native AAS constraint only; not an adopted DIM/Profile requirement or proof of schema enforcement.

original_constraint_items.native_meaning: A child semanticId, when present, must equal semanticIdListElement.
original_constraint_items.caveat: Native AAS constraint only; not an adopted DIM/Profile requirement or proof of schema enforcement.

original_constraint_items.native_meaning: First-level list children have the declared SubmodelElement type.
original_constraint_items.caveat: Native AAS constraint only; not an adopted DIM/Profile requirement or proof of schema enforcement.

original_constraint_items.native_meaning: Property/Range lists require valueTypeListElement and consistent child valueType.

original_items.title: Capability describes potential
original_items.native_meaning: Capability is an implementation-independent description of an asset potential to achieve a physical or virtual effect; the class adds no own attributes beyond inherited SubmodelElement information.
original_items.caveat: A capability declaration is not availability, execution, readiness or a measured achieved effect.

original_items.title: Capability-to-skill relationship
original_items.native_meaning: The note describes semantic relationship links from a capability to skills; typical implementations may use a property, operation, collection or whole submodel.
original_items.caveat: The external 2020 capabilities paper and ontology contents remain unread; no one-to-one capability/command mapping is established.

original_items.title: Operation description and invocation boundary
original_items.native_meaning: Operation describes input, output and inoutput variable lists; Part 1 points to Part 2 synchronous/asynchronous invocation. Instance and template operation specifications are handled identically.
original_items.caveat: This is a description of an interface; Part 2 execution, errors, acceptance/completion and cancellation contracts remain unreviewed.

original_items.title: Operation argument/result and future optionality
original_items.native_meaning: Each of the three variable lists is 0..*; each OperationVariable contains exactly one SubmodelElement value describing an argument/result. Default value and optional/mandatory cardinality on OperationVariable are mentioned as future extension examples.
original_items.caveat: The wrapper value cardinality is not proof that an operation argument is mandatory; do not invent the future fields or ISA parameter equivalence.

original_items.title: Experimental event model
original_items.native_meaning: The event concept remains experimental and future backward compatibility is not ensured.
original_items.caveat: Keep this standing on every event-derived mapping; it is not an adopted stable DIM event class.

original_items.title: Observed referable
original_items.native_meaning: BasicEventElement.observed is a required reference to a modeled Referable such as a data element or Submodel; direction is required input or output.
original_items.caveat: The observed target is an information-model object, not automatically a physical feature of interest or an OGC observation.

original_items.title: Event on/off state
original_items.native_meaning: BasicEventElement.state is required and uses StateOfEvent on/off literals.
original_items.caveat: This is the state of the event, not a device health taxonomy, selected operating mode or command readiness.

original_items.title: Event infrastructure hints
original_items.native_meaning: Optional messageTopic and messageBroker identify outer communication routing and a referable containing proprietary broker details; the note suggests possible standardized submodels.
original_items.caveat: This does not establish a configured transport, delivery guarantee, authorization or interoperability of the broker description.

original_items.title: Last event send or receive time
original_items.native_meaning: Optional lastUpdate is UTC time of the last event received for input direction or sent for output direction.
original_items.caveat: This is a last-event timestamp, not a timestamp on every exchange, a measured phenomenon time or general record modification time.

original_items.title: Minimum event interval
original_items.native_meaning: Optional minInterval limits maximum event frequency; input concerns the handling capability of the software entity, output concerns sending frequency to outer infrastructure.
original_items.caveat: Not a sensor sampling interval or automatically ISA minimum Status interval; absence means no minimum interval is specified.

original_items.title: Maximum output event interval
original_items.native_meaning: maxInterval is not applicable to input; for output it describes a maximum interval for sending an event-status update even without another trigger.
original_items.caveat: Not an operation to change the interval and not a universal component heartbeat or sensor reporting contract; source sentence contains awkward double-negative wording.

original_items.title: Event payload source and scope references
original_items.native_meaning: EventPayload requires source (event element) and observableReference (referable defining scope); semantic references for each are optional and external references are recommended.
original_items.caveat: No dedicated occurrence ID or original-event-to-copy lineage is supplied by these source/scope references.

original_items.title: Event trigger time
original_items.native_meaning: EventPayload.timestamp is required UTC time when the event was triggered.
original_items.caveat: Trigger time is not automatically physical phenomenon time, observation result time, or exchange send time; no leap/clock conformance is asserted.

original_items.title: Event initiator attribution
original_items.native_meaning: Optional subjectId identifies who or what initiated creation; the note calls it an external reference and assumes a unique subject identifier.
original_items.caveat: A field naming an initiator is not proof of authentication, authorization, evidence provenance or identity correctness; NIST ABAC reference remains unread.

original_items.title: Custom event type and payload
original_items.native_meaning: Event types use semanticId and specialized payloads; custom types may use proprietary worldwide-unique semantic IDs and customized payloads within the general event-message format.
original_items.caveat: The examples do not define a universal event-reason enumeration, detector snapshot, health vocabulary or complete transport protocol.

original_items.title: Condition, execution and audit event use cases
original_items.native_meaning: Firmware notices, condition-monitoring incidents, change tracking and cloud value push motivate event use. The later table also lists execution monitoring, infrastructure and security events.
original_items.caveat: Motivating use cases and illustrations do not supply mandatory execution-state, alarm, condition or history payload schemas.

original_items.title: Logical event scope
original_items.native_meaning: The event scope can cover an AAS, a Submodel and its logical dependents, a collection/list/entity and dependents, or one atomic element.
original_items.caveat: Logical scope is not physical equipment containment or a guarantee that all physical events are observed.

original_items.title: Condition values and value quality
original_items.native_meaning: Qualifier type/value adds context to values or semantics; semanticId is recommended. Generic properties may represent actual/runtime values and qualifiers can indicate measured or substitute value quality.
original_items.caveat: A generic carrier is not a standardized equipment operating-condition vocabulary or an authenticated current reading.

original_items.title: Administrative version and revision
original_items.native_meaning: AdministrativeInformation has optional version, revision, creator, createdAt and updatedAt; revision requires version through AASd-005.
original_items.caveat: Versions concern the identifiable information element, not automatically hardware, firmware or current sensor configuration.

original_items.title: Business creation/update milestones
original_items.native_meaning: createdAt remains tied to object identity; updatedAt tracks relevant modifications and cannot precede creation. The note treats version/revision/dates as business milestones and does not require updates for every transient data change.
original_items.caveat: These timestamps do not establish last acquisition, live freshness, connectivity or technical system modification time.

original_items.title: Distinguishing semantically similar submodels
original_items.native_meaning: Two Submodels with the same semanticId must be distinguished by the listed administrative/semantic alternatives; revision alone is ignored for the version alternative, and the stated presence conditions apply. Distinct Submodel IDs remain required.
original_items.caveat: Do not treat version, creator or dates as a universal asset identity rule; the no-semanticId/no-templateId note also limits formal comparison.

original_items.title: Creator and template provenance
original_items.native_meaning: creator identifies the subject responsible for making the information element; templateId identifies the template guiding its creation and is not the validation key, which uses semanticId.
original_items.caveat: A record creator/template identifier does not authenticate an assertion or identify an installed unit; preserve prior AAS02/AAS03 provenance distinctions.

original_items.title: Version representation inconsistency
original_items.native_meaning: Administration prose calls version/revision numerical integer types, but the datatype tables define one-to-four-character digit strings and the selected JSON definition also uses strings.
original_items.caveat: Do not silently choose an integer wire encoding or claim the source inconsistency resolved.

original_items.title: UTC example inconsistency
original_items.native_meaning: DateTimeUtc is defined for UTC but includes an example with +01:00 as well as a Z example; the selected administration JSON patterns allow only zero-offset suffixes.
original_items.caveat: The conflict is retained for AAS05 schema corroboration; no local timezone conversion or exhaustive regex validity is inferred.

original_items.title: Proprietary extension standing
original_items.native_meaning: HasExtensions permits proprietary extensions; the source explicitly says these do not support global interoperability.
original_items.caveat: Availability of an extension mechanism is not acceptance into a common vocabulary or ISA Custom/Nominated/Accepted governance status.

original_items.title: Extension fields and local names
original_items.native_meaning: Extension has required name, optional valueType defaulting to xs:string, optional value and zero-or-more refersTo model references; it inherits semantics. AASd-077 requires unique names within the owner.
original_items.caveat: Names and typed values do not establish shared meaning, validation of vendor content or global name uniqueness.

original_items.title: Proprietary and templated submodels
original_items.native_meaning: The annex permits standardized and proprietary information in the same infrastructure; public or non-public templates can guide instantiation with predefined semantics and source-defined cardinalities.
original_items.caveat: No selected industrial template or external dictionary has been audited in AAS04; interpreting unknown manufacturer semantics remains conditional.

original_items.title: Event timestamp spelling across source forms
original_items.native_meaning: Pinned local UML partial spells timeStamp, while the native attribute table uses timestamp.
original_items.caveat: Retain the native attribute-table spelling; rendering and full cross-schema reconciliation remain AAS05 concerns.

original_items.title: Changing value qualifiers and static context
original_items.native_meaning: ValueQualifier may vary over time and is restricted to instances; ConceptQualifier is static semantic context; TemplateQualifier is static template context, with source constraints and the operation-variable exception.
original_items.caveat: As-planned/as-maintained examples are semantic context, not actual maintenance state or proof of live data quality; external qualifier dictionaries remain unread.

original_items.native_meaning: Digital shell requires assetInformation, AssetInformation requires assetKind; optional global/specific asset ID is not installed equipment identity.
Reference requires type and keys, not proof of physical linkage or resolvable OGC URI.
Collection/List value optional, minItems 1 when present; list typeValueListElement required and orderRelevant optional.
Operation variable arrays optional, minItems 1 when present; OperationVariable.value required; not execution/mandatory argument semantics.
EventPayload JSON requires timeStamp and source/observableReference; text uses timestamp.
Administrative version/revision digit strings 1–4 chars; UTC dates zero-offset patterns.
Full-model Range valueType and optional lexical string min/max.
Extension requires local name; semantics/typed values not automatic global interoperability.
XML shell requires assetInformation; optional digital/reference links not physical attachment evidence.
XML Operation optional variable wrappers require one-or-more child OperationVariable, with value required.
XML EventPayload requires timeStamp, not text timestamp.
XML optional list/collection wrappers nonempty when present; no empty update equivalence.
Administrative versions constrained as digit strings in XML, versus integer prose.
OWL EventPayload/timeStamp data property string, contrary to native text spelling.
OWL says list ordered, but value ordinary object property; triple order/round trip not proven.
SHACL EventPayload/timeStamp minCount1/maxCount1 with UTC pattern; not verified physical event.
SHACL list value minCount0 with class SubmodelElement; no order container in selected shape.
Part2-shared Part1 schema requires EventPayload.timeStamp, as do native serializations.
Part2-shared metamodel Operation/OperationVariable structure declares arguments, not effects.
Shared full-model Range has valueType and optional string min/max.
API RangeValue requires numeric min and max, unlike full-model lexical optional pair.
Operation request/result value-only structures are schema envelopes, not executed action contracts.
ListValue array versus CollectionValue ValueOnly; no equivalence with RDF or absent-vs-empty update.

comparison_updates.clarification: JSON/XML require shell assetInformation; that digital record may represent a physical or software asset, not proof of an installed sensing System or CSAPI URI.
Reference keys and optional submodel/asset links do not corroborate actual physically attached constituents.
Normal schema Operation variable containers are declarative optional arrays (nonempty when present), not evidence of an issued request or physical effect.
OperationVariable.value is required, while value-only API argument envelopes are distinct; neither makes a specific argument mandatory.
Declared output/inoutput variables and API OperationResultValueOnly are structures, not completion, acknowledgment or physical result.
Full-model list/collection arrays require at least one child if present, SHACL list values can be absent, and RDF triples do not guarantee element order.
Full-model Range allows optional string-lexical min/max with valueType; API RangeValue requires both numeric endpoints. This is distinct representation scope, not a universal allowed-values rule.
List.orderRelevant exists in the metamodel; generic RDF value object properties/SHACL triple shapes do not prove lossless ordered-list conversion.

Normal JSON/XML omit empty array/wrappers but require nonempty supplied containers, while SHACL can represent zero values and API ValueOnly differs. Preserve supplied-empty versus omitted-update hold.
Experimental EventPayload text spells timestamp; JSON/XML/OWL/SHACL/shared OpenAPI spell timeStamp. Original source inconsistency unresolved; neither proves observation time.
Selected UTC patterns use zero offset while the DateTimeUtc original example allows a nonzero offset; neither establishes device clock synchronization.
Published prose calls administrative version/revision integers; selected JSON/XML/shared metamodel schemas use 1–4 digit strings. This is not installed firmware version.
Typed named extensions in the original schema retain vendor specificity; syntactic admissibility does not establish globally shared meaning or adopted Profile requirement.

AAS Registry, Repository, standalone Service and Discovery expose distinct 3.2 service profiles; Full, Read, Query, History and Signature do not imply the same mandatory command support.
/description profiles declare supported API-operation subsets; they are not an ISA equipment Config report or proof that commands are enabled and ready.
AAS Discovery -> Registry descriptor -> endpoint lookup is a source-defined software location chain, not a verified live physical network connection. Shell endpoint may be omitted.
AAS profile URI/version and HTTP serialization modifiers describe available API representation choices; versioned URL prefix and identity encoding are not guaranteed common CSAPI framing.
AAS and Submodel descriptors can expose separate endpoints but are not an observed source of installed component hierarchy or producer-origin equipment attribution.
Optional repository JWS retrieval concerns a digital-shell representation; it does not independently verify the source publisher, NOAA record, or an authenticated factual assertion.
Repository record-at-date history explicitly differs from AdministrativeInformation.version and from a physical component's current configuration/firmware version.
Protocol securityAttributes, generic 401/403 failure codes and optional JWS representation are not ISA request-user authorization metadata or verified issuer authentication.
Generic API HTTP 200/202/4xx statuses and Result objects can acknowledge software requests but do not establish sensing-device command completion, physical effect or ISA outcome.

original_items.native_meaning: Submodel Interface separates reads, path/file updates and operation invocation from actual equipment.
GetSubmodel and element-list operations read model information, not a performed observation.
PatchSubmodel updates a model; metadata-only content retains existing values.
PatchSubmodelElementByPath addresses model content, not physical equipment.
Get/Patch SubmodelElementValueByPath use ValueOnly model values; no physical sampling proven.
InvokeOperationSync accepts optional arguments and returns OperationResult, not physical actuation evidence.
InvokeOperationAsync returns handle; server may disregard client's suggested timeout.
Async operation status and result retrieval are separate API calls.
OperationRequest arguments and ValueOnly variants are distinct representation shapes.
BaseOperationResult executionState/optional success differs from OperationResult output variables.
Initiated, Running, Completed, Canceled, Failed, Timeout and OperationHandle describe invocation lifecycle.
HTTP 202 may precede invalid/failed invocation, 302 leads to result, HTTP 200 can carry Failed.
AASX File Server manages packages separately from instantiated Submodel or AAS.
GetAASXByPackageId returns package bytes and filename.
PostAASXPackage may store package+IDs without parsing/instantiating.
Put/Delete AASX packages are file management, not sensor configuration.
AASX Async upload has separate handle/status/result.
/packages-async initial 202 does not guarantee eventual success.
Submodel Registry records descriptors/endpoints separate from model bodies.
Submodel Registry list/get descriptors offer date filters, cursor and limit.
PostSubmodelDescriptor registers an endpoint descriptor, not device.
QuerySubmodelDescriptors searches AAS records, not ISA message subscriptions.
SubmodelDescriptor ID/endpoint required; semantic reference optional.
Submodel Repository stores digital Submodels and supports semantic/date queries.
GetAllSubmodelsRecentChanges is Experimental business-record change list.
History-by-date differs from AdministrativeInformation.version, version triggers undefined.
semanticId and supplementalSemanticId source matching is not external ontology proof.
Post/Put/Patch Submodels change digital records, not verified firmware/hardware.
QuerySubmodels is a model record query, not ISA message matching.
Signed Submodel JWS does not verify issuer by existence alone.
ConceptDescription Repository supports definition records and isCaseOf/dataSpecification filters.
Concept Description recent changes Experimental; list dates not live observation time.
Submodel Service Full/Read/Value differ; Value SSP003 includes synchronous POST invocation.
AASX Async profile lists InvokeOperationAsync but pinned YAML has PostAsyncAASXPackage.
Submodel Registry Query SSP004 Name says Bulk, but profile URI is Query.
Submodel Repository Read SSP002 text uses SubmodelServiceSpecification instead of SubmodelRepository URI.
Template SSP003/004 prohibit kind Instance; text misnames some SubmodelService profile references.
AASa-003/004 prohibit Template Repository profiles accepting/providing kind=Instance.
Submodel Repository Query/Signature/History profiles separate, history is model as-of date.
ConceptDescription Repository Full/Query/Signature profiles are distinct optional APIs.
Value SSP003 uses POST /invoke and /invoke/$value with different request/result schemas.
Full Submodel Service includes asynchronous invoke/status/result paths.
Template SSP003 GET /submodels filters IDs/semantics; AASa003 governs template-only restriction.
History SSP007 GET /submodels/{submodelIdentifier}/$history with optional date.
Submodel Registry Query SSP004 POST /query/submodel-descriptors.
ConceptDescription Full SSP001 lists by idShort/isCaseOf/dataSpecificationRef.
ConceptDescription Query SSP002 POST /query/concept-descriptions.
ConceptDescription Signature SSP003 returns a JWS string.
AASX Full SSP001 multipart binary package storage need not parse.
AASX Async SSP002 POST /packages-async accepts multipart file.
AASX async status/result schema uses BaseOperationResult vs interface OperationResult.
BaseOperationResult fields executionState/success do not guarantee physical outcome.
Normal/ValueOnly and asynchronous OperationRequest/Result encodings differ.

comparison_updates.clarification: Submodel Registry/Repository/Service, ConceptDescription Repository and AASX profile subsets are API roles, not ISA mandatory equipment command roles.
Submodel Value profile includes synchronous POST invocation while Read does not; advertised API support does not prove equipment readiness.
Submodel descriptors provide IDs and service endpoints, not physical connection or sensor network presence.
Normal/Metadata/ValueOnly and nested idShortPath API representations differ by Submodel profile, not a universal CSAPI transport envelope.
Model-declared Operation can be invoked synchronously/asynchronously but is not a proven ISA equipment command catalogue.
OperationRequest input/inoutput and ValueOnly encodings differ; async timeout may be required yet server may disregard requested timing.
OperationResult and native executionState characterize API business operation, not verified ISA device outcome.
POST /invoke and /invoke-async define interfaces, not evidence the device actually received an issued command.
HTTP 202 Accepted may be followed by failure; HTTP 200 with executionState Failed is not a successful physical command effect.
Initiated/Running/Completed/Canceled/Failed/Timeout and OperationHandle are API lifecycle, not a source-authenticated hardware execution record.
Template-only Submodel repository profiles explicitly exclude kind Instance, so templates do not establish installed equipment structure.
Submodel PATCH/ValueOnly do not resolve earlier normal-JSON supplied-empty versus omitted update distinction.
Template repository can represent designed fields without establishing an instantiated sensing System or actual values.
Submodel history-as-of-date is not AdministrativeInformation.version or sensor firmware and RecentChanges is experimental.
ConceptDescription semantic records/signatures do not imply accepted global vocabulary or verified external IEC meaning.
Optional Submodel/ConceptDescription JWS retrieval does not independently authenticate manufacturer or NOAA original-source facts.
ValueOnly Submodel retrieval is a digital data property, not evidence of an actual observation emitted by equipment.
ValueOnly model-element read/write envelope differs from ISA named-value message representation.
Native Submodel list, template and ValueOnly paths do not establish ISA list-order or RDF conversion equivalence.
AAS record queries select Submodels, descriptors or ConceptDescriptions, not ISA message-matching subscriptions.
Asynchronous server operation status is not a sensing component property-value Status message or physical condition.
AASX packages may be stored without parsing and are not ISA ZIP archives of original historical result records.

original_items.native_meaning: IEC61360 is a data specification for concept definitions of properties, values and value lists; template identity is separate from ConceptDescription identity. The template uses major-version /3 while its attributes use /3/1; deprecated alternate template IRIs remain listed.

preferredName is required; shortName, unit, unitId, sourceOfDefinition, symbol and dataType have optional class cardinality, subject to cross-constraints. unit and unitId must agree if both supplied. They describe concepts, not observed equipment.

definition, valueFormat, valueList, value and levelType describe concept semantics; template value is a coded-value definition, not a measurement sample. ConceptDescription id/version and display/description are distinct from similar template fields.
19 native datatype literals distinguish measure/count/currency, translatable text, identifiers, file addresses and binary content. These do not constitute a sensor observable catalogue.

LevelType min/nom/typ/max are required Boolean availability flags, not numeric bound values. The note describes Property, Range or Collection mappings and discourages level types except ranges; it cannot resolve ISA Level or adopt a DIM representation.

ValueList contains one or more valueReferencePair entries; pair value is required and valueId optional. If both supplied, the lexical value must agree with the referenced concept. No general include/exclude restriction algebra is supplied.

AAS maps IEC datatypes to XSD or element forms: rational values to strings; real measures to float or double; translatable strings to MultiLanguageProperty; FILE to File, BLOB/HTML to Blob. Native semantic type is not identical to encoded value type.

ConceptDescription category is deprecated in Part1. The category tables are recommendations for legacy usage, not an adopted class hierarchy. Their preferredName footnote recommends English while constraint AASc-3a-002 requires English; retain the standing difference.

Template primitive limits differ: definition strings 1–1023, preferred names 1–255 (35 advised), short names 1–18, values 1–2048. XML/JSON/RDF serialization is delegated to Part1; no new whole-schema conformance claim.
preferredName shall include English.
A referenced IEC61360 value ConceptDescription shall define value.
Legacy PROPERTY/VALUE categories require the specified property/value datatype subset.
Legacy REFERENCE category restricts datatype to STRING, IRI or IRDI.
Legacy DOCUMENT category restricts datatype to FILE, BLOB or HTML.
Legacy QUALIFIER_TYPE category requires datatype.
definition is mandatory in English except for a concept that defines value.
Measure and currency datatypes require unit or unitId.
value and valueList are mutually exclusive when nonempty; both may be empty as explained in the class note.
Use of the template requires the corresponding external template reference ending /3.

Part3b covers minimal interpretation metadata for an existing unit (use case 2). Part3a alone can name a unit; complete user-defined unit definitions (use case 3) are out of scope. Equal unit symbols/dimensions do not establish equal quantities; energy and torque illustrate the distinction.

Part3a unitId references a ConceptDescription carrying the units template. Property semanticId identifies the property concept; unitId identifies the unit concept. The controller-height diagram is synthetic and uses DataSpecificationUnitOfMeasurement, unlike normative DataSpecificationUoM naming.

When only semanticId is supplied, use the dictionary primary/default unit; without a dictionary default, supply a ConceptDescription defining unit/unitId. A supplied ConceptDescription unit takes precedence. Same property semantics with different units requires distinct ConceptDescription identities/isCaseOf and is discouraged due to complexity; no conversion algorithm is specified.

ConceptDescription id should use the global unit identifier when available; otherwise choose an id and record the classification-system identifier in specificUnitID. A short local unit code alone is not global concept identity.

Eight unit attributes: preferredName and symbol required; specificUnitID, definition, preferredNameQuantity, quantityId, classificationSystem and classificationSystemVersion optional. Quantity name/id must agree; select exactly one applicable quantity for the property purpose. Preserve quantityId versus quantityID spelling difference.

Units strings/names use 1–256 characters; definitions/identifiers 1–2048. The source delegates serialization to Part1 and links datatype v3.1 despite index targeting v3.2; companion versions are not one uniform v3.2 document.

The annex recommends one actually consulted dictionary and coherent version, not mixed attributes from unrelated dictionaries. Its ECLASS and IEC CDD mappings are publisher examples, not independent audits of those external dictionaries.

Negative examples reject mixed-source unit metadata and a non-global MMT concept identifier without classification-system context. Table symbol cardinality 0 conflicts with required symbol in the normative template; do not adopt the example as a rule.

Part4 describes exchangeable access rules and technology-neutral/specific security. It does not prescribe one identity-management solution; Type3 active agents are out of scope. AASX can carry a proposed Security Model, whose enforcement belongs to the recipient system.

File import crosses security domains; a recipient establishes its own access rights. Repositories protect stored AAS content, registries protect descriptors. Policy administration, decision, enforcement and attribute-information functions are distinct; dataspace trust/claims policies are additional agreements.

Integrity, confidentiality and availability priorities are risk-dependent. Requirements protect data, structure, services and their asset relation; these are security obligations, not evidence that a particular implementation meets them.

Seven foundational areas address AAS structure/interfaces. Authentication and identifier policy are required for protected access; template-guided input validation is recommended. Audit events S1–S4 are required, A1–A3 conditionally required for accountability, timestamps at least seconds; machine-readable audit is required. Log-as-submodel and asset-root distribution are possibilities, not mandatory field definitions.

Attributes need trustworthy/authenticated sources; a valid true rule permits the designated action/object, otherwise default deny. Implementations may support subsets, choose internal representation, and should follow this model if exchanging rules. No uniform runtime conformance is inferred.

Signed JWT bearer tokens convey authenticated subject claims. Dataspace policy defines trusted tokens and attributes; standard iss/exp/aud/sub/client_id/iat/jti claims are identified. Lifetime/Proof-of-Possession choices are recommendations tied to use case. Claims and expiry are not hardware identity or observation validity.

An access rule combines ACL, protected objects and a Boolean formula, optionally fragment FILTER/FILTERLIST. Reusable attribute/object/ACL/formula definitions are supported. SubmodelElement visibility requires both element and parents visible; this is returned-data visibility, not physical composition.

Rights CREATE/READ/UPDATE/DELETE/EXECUTE/VIEW/ALL depend on the target operation, not HTTP method alone. VIEW exposes existence without value; ALLOW grants when true and DISABLED is ignored. Normative per-operation mapping is delegated to Part2; no new all-operation audit.

CLAIM, GLOBAL and REFERENCE attributes differ. LOCALNOW/UTCNOW/CLIENTNOW need trustworthy time and ANONYMOUS denotes no token. A REFERENCE may consult a different model context, such as machine state, but is still model data, not independent sensor truth.

Protected objects include routes, Identifiable, Referable, Fragment and Descriptor. ROUTE matching uses path only, exact path or suffix wildcard prefix; six field prefixes distinguish shell/submodel/element/concept/descriptor contexts. No equipment attachment or task-routing identity follows.

Boolean conditions, typed comparisons, string operations, casts and match are defined; arithmetic is unsupported. Undefined attributes or evaluation errors make the formula false. Typed field conversion skips unconvertible values; all failed conversion yields false. These are access/query predicates, not observation processing algorithms.

JSON syntax accompanies BNF, but lexical date/time patterns do not reject impossible calendar dates. Time without timezone must be interpreted UTC and serialized Z. Schema validation alone cannot demonstrate policy evaluation, calendar validity or access enforcement.

Rule serialization support is optional, JSON recommended, enforcement implementation-specific. A manufacturer can propose rules for the recipient to adapt; rules may be stored as FILE/BLOB payload. Transferring rules does not grant operational permissions.

No native data-bound protection of arbitrary AAS elements is specified. Accountability combines access control, audits and transit protection; /$signed supplies a basic API mechanism. Signed payloads are possible, with syntax/semantics defined by the AAS Responsible; verified integrity is not verified truth of an equipment claim.

globalAssetId/specificAssetIds association is unprotected and may be attacked. IEEE802.1AR identities could support stronger identification, but this text does not define an adopted device-certificate field or complete secure-binding mechanism.

Original JSON contract requires rules, ACL-or-USEACL, objects-or-reference and formula-or-reference; additional properties are restricted. RIGHTS array lacks minItems although BNF requires at least one Right. No grammar/schema equivalence claimed.

Original BNF defines reusable rule groups, attributes, objects, formulas, lexical types and field identifiers. It requires one or more rights; its lexical syntax and date checks do not establish behavioral enforcement.
Publisher example grants READ/UPDATE on a named Submodel when a token email claim matches. It is illustrative rule data, not an observed authorization decision or an equipment command.

Publisher example conditions maintenance-document visibility on referenced machineState. Its reusable ACL lists role but the formula also refers to machineState; undeclared-attribute false rule leaves declaration/evaluation semantics needing clarification, not evidence of working enforcement.

AASX is a file-exchange container between partners; export/import may filter information. Logical file relationships and physical ZIP directory structure describe a package, not physical assembly of sensors. The policy-not-submitted wording differs from Part4 optional rule payload exchange and needs interpretation by context.

AASX serializes complete or partial AAS information with selected supplementary files. It uses .aasx and application/aas+zip, an aasx-origin entry, and Open Packaging Conventions reserved paths. File-server acceptance alone does not prove package validity.

Thumbnail and core-properties describe the package. aasx-origin is required; aas-spec references serialized Identifiable content in one or more representations. Core title/creator/revision are not automatically equipment or AAS record metadata.

aas-suppl targets extra files referenced through relative File URIs; Blob values are not supplementary files. Source is the serialized AAS file, and multiple serializations need corresponding relationships. Table 0..1 cardinality versus plural text/changelog is held, not silently generalized.

Relationships locate content regardless of filename; aasx/ and origin conventions use shall, data.<extension> uses should. Same data can be serialized XML/JSON side by side; this does not duplicate the real event or prove lossless equivalence.
When signing to protect AAS data, relevant origin, structure, supplementary files and associated relationship parts shall be signed. Trust/verification is not furnished by archive presence.

ZIP encryption is prohibited as reported by Part5; external encryption or replacement encrypted content can be used with declared types. Packaging/relationship files remain unencrypted; sign after individual-content encryption, before whole-package encryption. This is Part5 guidance, not an independent ISO/cryptography audit.

Pinned v3.2 changelog identifies new application/aas+zip MIME type and removal of legacy format mentions; v3.1 entries cover extension names and sample archive. Release notes repeat older changes, so pin normative content rather than infer changes from release prose.

Pinned v3.2 index prints July2027 and history says this version3.1. GitHub release v3.2.0 was published 2026-07-21 as Release26-01. Preserve contradictory date/history; no future publication date substituted for release evidence.

comparison_updates.clarification: Part3a concept-definition metadata now inspected: names, source, semantic datatype, unit/unitId, definition and value-list rules; Part3b supplies a separate unit concept with quantity and dictionary/version context. These do not define ISA publication/mutability rules. Explicit concept units take precedence over dictionary defaults; conversion behavior remains unproved.
IEC61360 defines property meaning and units, not a complete declaration of sensor observables or an assurance that an Event occurs. Quantities must retain their subject and semantic identity.

Concept definitions can qualify field meaning with language names, definition/source and datatype. Optional class attributes are subject to English-definition and unit constraints; no ISA field-omission equivalence follows.

IEC61360 semantic datatypes differ from XSD/element encodings: rational becomes string; real may be float/double; multilingual/file/blob meanings use different elements. This is not ISA built-in/custom code equivalence.

valueList describes allowed coded values with optional valueId; template value/valueList are mutually exclusive when populated. LevelType flags describe available MIN/NOM/TYP/MAX roles, not numeric bounds or ISA include/exclude rules. Deprecated category recommendations stay qualified.

DataSpecificationIec61360.value describes a semantic coded value; it is not a measured Property.value. Preserve separate value-list identity and unit concept context when interpreting an instance value.

Part3a/3b can supply datatype, unit identity and quantity context for an instance measurement. Their templates do not supply this row’s uncertainty convention or prove any reported measurement; complete new-unit definitions and automatic conversion are outside the reviewed contract.

Part3b explicitly separates quantity from unit: shared units do not establish shared quantity. Property semanticId and unitId identify different concepts. Existing air/panel temperature and particulate case meanings remain distinct; no sensor observable dictionary was independently audited.

Part4 access rules combine authenticated claims/global/reference attributes, ACL rights, protected objects and Boolean conditions. Default deny, optional serialization and implementation-specific enforcement do not equal ISA request metadata or an observed grant. BNF/JSON minimum-rights discrepancy is held.

Part4 token trust depends on issuer keys and dataspace policy; signatures support integrity under that trust. Proposed IEEE802.1AR asset binding is a possible approach, not a defined required certificate field or proof of this physical equipment’s identity.
Part4 says globalAssetId/specificAssetIds binding is unprotected and attackable. A shell identifier or authenticated API token alone does not verify the identity of the described physical System.

Access-rule FILTER/FILTERLIST restrict returned fragments; element visibility also depends on visible parents. This is security selection of AAS data and descriptors, not the same message-query context or a physical hierarchy.

Part5 logical relationships/physical ZIP hierarchy organize files. Co-packaging shells, submodels and supplementary documents establishes no physical constituent relationship among equipment. Existing physical examples remain separate.

Part3a sourceOfDefinition and Part3b dictionary/version metadata support definition provenance, while Part4 audits/signatures support accountability under stated trust. Neither establishes the proposed complete source/issuer/edition/evidence record or truth of a physical claim.

AASX can carry several serializations of the same data and filtered partner exports. Package creator/revision belong to the package; they do not identify the original observation or prove lineage of Bennett experimental copies.

Part5 AASX is a selected AAS-content/supplementary-file exchange container, distinct from ISA’s ZIP of an archived-message result set. Package storage or sample archive presence proves neither valid content nor message history completeness.

AASX MIME type application/aas+zip and parallel XML/JSON serializations identify package/representation choices, not negotiated ISA presentation/schema pairs. Companion editions stay 3a3.1.1/3b3.0/Part4 3.1/Part5 3.2; source naming/date conflicts remain explicit.

original_items.native_meaning: Property constraints apply to properties of a single capability, using pre/invariant/post combinations and links to constrained properties. Operation, OCL, basic and custom alternatives have different representations; custom semantics remain unspecified.

original_items.access_grade: FULLY READ — cited text/table or explicitly selected native fields
original_items.native_meaning: Transition constraints relate the constrained capability to another capability with temporal pre/invariant/post combinations. They describe dependencies rather than an observed execution sequence or command result.

original_items.access_grade: FULLY READ — cited text/table or explicitly selected native fields
original_items.native_meaning: Three named constraints require consistent first-level list types, a nonempty choice of constraint-container kinds, and agreement between chosen constraint representation and ConstraintType. The specification says these restrictions are not explicitly modeled in the accompanying template.

comparison_updates.clarification: IDTA02003 v2.0 provides manufacturer name for product technical descriptions; its use case also treats a supplier as manufacturer. This is not the current operator or proof of an instance identity.

TechnicalData distinguishes product designation text, manufacturer article number and order code. These help identify a product offering; none is automatically a reusable model identifier or individual serial.

The reviewed TechnicalData general-information fields identify manufacturer/product/order data, not an individual hardware serial. Base hierarchy placeholder globalAssetIds must not be used as serials; other nameplate templates remain unreviewed.

Engineering reference designations are aspect/context dependent; rules for distributed asset-ID derivation are outside IDTA02011-1. Template semantic IDs and example globalAssetIds do not establish persistent identity of actual equipment.

Hierarchy, technical-data and capability templates describe an asset at type or instance level and may represent designs or requirements. Their combined information does not select a universal sensing-System root class.

IDTA02011 supplies logical asset HasPart/IsPartOf hierarchy and distinguishes co/self-managed entities. Lifecycle/design context and BulkCount type quantities prevent automatic interpretation as individually installed physical constituents; capability composition is functional.

Base hierarchy relations do not establish a cable/interface connection. More detailed physical connections and anchors are future extensions; Dragino external SHT31 and Campbell SDI-12 connections remain distinct from physical containment.

LocationAspect can describe a planned or actual location, and LocatedAt targets a LocationAspectNode. This contextual representation supplies neither surveyed probe coordinates nor proof that a station hosts installed equipment.

Full/OneDown/OneUp describe differently distributed logical hierarchies. Their relations may model intended structure and cannot by themselves establish a reported physical attachment; SameAs links representations, not attachment.

CapabilitySet groups function descriptions for a use case, with capability/property containers and relations. This resembles contextual grouping, but does not establish ISA categories or membership semantics for property/observable/command declarations.

IDTA02020 capabilities are required/offered/unassigned industrial functions with properties, constraints and skill links. This differs from ISA component capability catalogues of properties, observables, commands and types; skill binding remains incomplete.

TechnicalData provides dictionary-qualified or manufacturer-specific technical properties in readable sections and application descriptions. Classification does not prove property-set completeness, and human grouping alone is not machine semantics.

Capability property ranges and property/transition constraints describe applicability and temporal dependencies. They are not necessarily ISA included/excluded numeric endpoints or actual measured limits; native choice/cardinality conflicts remain held.

TechnicalData uses collections/lists for technical and application descriptions; CapabilityPropertyType has specific alternatives and list constraints. These are source-specific value organizations, not physical composition or adopted universal list/tree bounds.

TechnicalData defines multilingual display-name and concept-name fallbacks, with an unresolved repeated preferredName tier. Presentation labels do not establish the ability to change an equipment component name through a command.

CapabilityRealizedBy points toward a skill but does not issue a control request. OperationConstraint evaluates a condition and cannot execute in a file-only exchange; no device command or execution was tested.
Required/Offered/NotAssigned qualify the role of a function description; constraints describe applicability. Neither is the ISA ready/report-selection state or an observed live readiness report.

TechnicalData property values and capability ranges can describe specifications or examples. Their presence is not a measurement event or uncertainty contract; the publisher sample does not establish sensor behavior.

Manufacturer TextStatement and its invalid-from ValidDate provide assertion/validity context. They do not supply a complete evidence record or establish the truth of an installed-equipment assertion; template source/edition conflicts remain explicit.

Capability descriptions can support process planning with required functions and temporal dependencies. Those abstract plans are distinct from a sensing procedure, actual observation or evidence that a sequence executed.

source_to_master_changes.after: AAS09: PARTIAL — IDTA02003 v2.0 provides manufacturer name for product technical descriptions; its use case also treats a supplier as manufacturer. This is not the current operator or proof of an instance identity. [AAS09-N014, AAS09-N015]

F3_02_ISA_classification.peer_difference: Other donor responses must retain their own result/status meaning; transport, authorization decision and achieved hardware effect are separate.
F3_02_ISA_classification.negative_equivalence_boundary: Response code is a reported execution state not independent evidence of physical effect; even authorization denial can carry SUCCESS in its separate service context.

F3_05_AAS_classification.rationale: The API defines acceptance, execution state and result retrieval. Promote to a common qualified acknowledgement/outcome candidate: 202 can precede failure, and 200 with executionState Failed is a failed business operation. Hardware effect is not proved by transport success.

after.label: Command acknowledgement / reported outcome
after.definition: ACCEPTED is not COMPLETED, and COMPLETED is not measured physical effect.
display: [COMMON CANDIDATE] PARTIAL/RELATED: The API separates receipt, execution state and reported business success. A 202 response can precede failure; HTTP 200 with executionState Failed reports invocation failure. Optional success separately describes the business operation. Neither transport success nor a reported result proves physical effect. Preserve the executionState prose/schema requiredness conflict. [Sources: AAS07-N008, AAS07-N010, AAS07-N011, AAS07-N012, AAS07-N052; O5-S06-R020]

records.native_meaning: Protected objects include routes, Identifiable, Referable, Fragment and Descriptor. ROUTE matching uses path only, exact path or suffix wildcard prefix; six field prefixes distinguish shell/submodel/element/concept/descriptor contexts. No equipment attachment or task-routing identity follows.
records.rationale: Route/Identifiable/Referable/Fragment/Descriptor are policy target contexts. Native path prefixes, suffix wildcard and parent visibility do not establish physical hierarchy or task routing.

records.native_meaning: Boolean conditions, typed comparisons, string operations, casts and match are defined; arithmetic is unsupported. Undefined attributes or evaluation errors make the formula false. Typed field conversion skips unconvertible values; all failed conversion yields false. These are access/query predicates, not observation processing algorithms.

records.native_meaning: Rule serialization support is optional, JSON recommended, enforcement implementation-specific. A manufacturer can propose rules for the recipient to adapt; rules may be stored as FILE/BLOB payload. Transferring rules does not grant operational permissions.

records.native_meaning: No native data-bound protection of arbitrary AAS elements is specified.
